canonicalReview.reconciliationSummary: Two reviewers split: epic-reviewer-1 (claude-code) returned pass with five non-blocking findings; epic-reviewer-2 (codex) returned block with two majors, both verified dynamically. Independent re-verification against the code confirms both blockers, so the conservative rule holds and neither is downgraded. (1) Mode isolation: both reviewers found the same defect — reviewer-1 as minor E02-NB-002, reviewer-2 as blocking EPIC-02-BLOCK-001. Code confirms it: sdk.ts:254-257 installs the process-global scheduler poke and thread-touch seams only in background mode and manual mode 'leaves the slots alone'; shared/context.ts:40-48 holds module-global slots that nothing clears; work-queue enqueue (index.ts:136) unconditionally registers onCommit(() => fireSchedulerPoke(threadId)). A manual SDK constructed after a background SDK therefore drains automatically through the stale background scheduler, violating AC-1.7's manual-mode contract. The sdk.ts comment explicitly contemplates multi-SDK-per-process (background supersedes background), so the background-then-manual sequence is inside the design's contemplated space, not an unsupported configuration. The two findings are merged into one blocking finding; reviewer-1's minor classification is the material disagreement, resolved conservatively toward the dynamically verified blocker. (2) Deleted-pair outcomes: only reviewer-2 found EPIC-02-BLOCK-002, and every step of its claimed code path verifies: findPairedBlock (messages/internal/forms.ts:163-178) joins message with no deleted_at IS NULL filter — an unsanctioned exception to tech-design Part 3b's deleted-read filter rule, which names exactly two exceptions, neither of them the pairing read; toolCallSummaryHandler (handlers.ts:98-105) stamps outcome from that unfiltered read, so a tool_call_summary requeued after its paired result is deleted rebuilds outcome 'succeeded' from a record no longer in the readable record (against AC-2.4's no-paired-result→unknown and AC-6.1); cascadeMessageDelete (cascade.ts:209-215) drops the deleted message's own forms and clears upward only, never touching the paired counterpart's summary; and compose.ts:150-153 prefers the ready summary's stale metadata over its own mechanical outcomeFromRecord fallback, so the delete cascade's own rendering rebuild republishes the stale outcome. This partially invalidates reviewer-1's cross-story claim that the deleted-read filter is applied at every read site with only sanctioned exceptions. There is genuine spec tension behind the cascade half — AC-6.2's 'nothing else changes' excludes the counterpart summary from the cascade while AC-2.8 establishes the pair as the summary's source — carried as an unresolved item needing a human ruling; the missing read filter is an unambiguous defect regardless of that ruling. Reviewer-1's remaining non-blocking findings (E02-NB-001 wall-clock in mutations confirmed at five runInTransaction(db, () => new Date()) sites; E02-NB-003 deterministic-only registry confirmed in providers/registry.ts; E02-NB-004 thrown-handler-to-retryable confirmed at scheduler.ts:139-145; E02-NB-005 attempts asymmetry confirmed at scheduler.ts:119-125 vs 158-165) are all supported and retained. Epic gate re-run independently: pnpm run verify-all exit 0 (build, typecheck, lint, boundaries, 29 test files, 231 tests) — a passing gate does not offset the confirmed blockers, since the missing coverage (cross-SDK mode isolation, delete of a paired tool result) is exactly why the suite stays green.
crossStoryFindings: Confirmed: manual/background mode isolation does not survive SDK sequencing within one process. Background-mode construction installs process-global scheduler poke and thread-touch seams (sdk.ts:254-257, shared/context.ts:40-48) that a later manual-mode SDK never clears, and every enqueue unconditionally fires the global poke post-commit (work-queue/index.ts:136), so work queued through a manual SDK drains automatically through the leftover background scheduler — with that scheduler's provider and config — without any drain call.

Confirmed: the deletion flow does not compose with paired tool-call/tool-result derivation. The pairing read crosses the deleted-read filter discipline (findPairedBlock has no deleted_at filter), the delete cascade never clears the paired counterpart's tool_call_summary even though AC-2.8 makes the pair the summary's source, and turn-rendering composition (compose.ts:150-153) trusts the stale ready summary's metadata over its own record-derived fallback — so a deleted tool result's outcome survives into rebuilt renderings and even into an explicit post-delete requeue of the summary.

The story chain otherwise composes into one coherent mechanism: enqueue is the single creation point for derived_form rows, completion is UPDATE-only and source-version-checked, handlers return form writes as data, report/requeue join live work_item rows, and all three mutations reuse the identical enqueue/supersede/version machinery through the one shared cascade module (DD-8), with turns.deleteTurn reaching it only via the messages domain's public surface.

The deleted-read filter rule is applied at the membership and read-back sites introduced across Stories 3-6 (message reads, member projections, chunk rows, turn reads), but reviewer-1's claim that every read site complies with only sanctioned exceptions is corrected by the confirmed blocker: the call-id pairing read is an unfiltered read of message content that the tech design's two-exception list does not sanction.

Work-item identity (w-<sourceId>-<kind>-v<sourceVersion>), the DD-1 five-disposition contract, and the DD-3 stale-discard truth table hold consistently across intake queueing, drain, repair requeues, and the mutation cascade's replacement enqueues.
architectureFindings: Confirmed drift from the architecture contract: mode selection is declared per SDK instance (DD-4: hosts see mode at construction) but enforced through process-global mutable hooks, so the mode contract is only as strong as the last background construction in the process; manual mode's AC-1.7 guarantee is not enforceable by the manual instance itself. The fix needs a small design decision — clear the slots on manual construction, scope the seams per SDK instance, or refuse multi-SDK construction — though all variants are mechanically small.

Confirmed: the deleted-read filter discipline (tech design Part 3b) misses the tool pairing read path, and the mutation cascade's scope (derived structurally from the message→turn→chunk walk in cascade.ts) cannot reach the paired counterpart's summary, which the derivation architecture (AC-2.8, outcome stamping from the pair) makes a real source dependency. The epic's own cascade-scope table ('nothing else changes') conflicts with the pair-as-source model AC-2.8 introduced — a spec-level gap, not just an implementation one.

Module placement otherwise matches the tech design with two approved, recorded renames (turn handlers in turns/internal/derive.ts; scheduler seams in shared/context.ts to avoid an import cycle, DD-5 semantics preserved); migration v5 implements the schema faithfully including the F-02 backfill; claimNext is the single atomic UPDATE under BEGIN IMMEDIATE with structural never-skip-ahead; provider calls never run inside a transaction; the DD-9 chunk close policy reads only stored projected-token values, which is what makes TC-3.9 replay determinism hold.

Minor drift retained from reviewer-1: createSdk's injected clock governs drain and scheduler timestamps, but mutation and requeue operations construct their own wall clock (five runInTransaction(db, () => new Date(), ...) sites in messages/index.ts and turns/index.ts), so deterministic time injection does not extend to the mutation surfaces (E02-NB-001).
epicCoverageAssessment: Epic gate independently re-run for this canonical review: pnpm run verify-all from packages/lhc exits 0 — build, typecheck, lint (75 files), boundary check, and 29 test files / 231 tests all green, including the LHC_PROCESS_SUITE spawned-process fixtures (TC-1.3 SIGKILL restart survival, TC-1.4 cross-process claim exclusion).

All 46 TC ids appear verbatim in test titles and all 47 ACs trace to implemented behavior per reviewer-1's file-level audit; the four architecture-risk tests named by the test plan (TC-1.3, TC-1.4, TC-5.4, TC-3.9) are present and green; CLI parity surfaces call the same domain operations with the same validation and result JSON.

Two coverage gaps correspond exactly to the confirmed blockers: no test constructs a background SDK followed by a manual SDK in one process (the AC-1.7 isolation case), and no test deletes or edits a tool result whose paired call summary already landed (the AC-2.4/AC-6.2 pairing case). Both blockers' fix paths must add these tests.
productionPathFindings: No fake adapters, stubs, placeholders, or silent provider defaults: CLI drain requires --provider or LHC_PROVIDER and fails closed with provider_not_configured; the deterministic provider is explicit-only per DD-11 and is currently the sole registered named provider (real adapters are an explicit epic scope exclusion — operators need a future adapter registration for real inference; E02-NB-003).

Material production-path issue confirmed: in any process that ever constructed a background SDK, a subsequently constructed manual SDK silently behaves as background — its enqueues drain through the stale scheduler with the prior SDK's provider and config (EPIC-02-BLOCK-001).

Material production-path issue confirmed: the tool pairing read returns deleted messages, so production drains and explicit requeues can land ready forms whose mechanically stamped outcomes derive from records outside the readable record (EPIC-02-BLOCK-002).

Test seams compiled into production modules (intake walk hook/clock, scheduler testPassCount) are inert in production assembly and documented in place; background scheduling is gated fail-closed on hasAnyHandler; thrown handler errors are deliberately softened to retryable attempts to keep the queue from wedging (scheduler.ts:139-145, E02-NB-004).

blockingFindings.title: Manual SDK mode can auto-drain after background SDK construction in the same process
blockingFindings.evidence: Confirmed in code (and dynamically by epic-reviewer-2; reviewer-1 independently found the same defect as E02-NB-002). createSdk installs the process-wide seams only for background mode and manual mode leaves them installed (packages/lhc/src/sdk.ts:254-257: installSchedulerPoke / setThreadTouch under `if (resolved.mode === "background")`, with the comment documenting only background-supersedes-background); the slots are module globals nothing else clears (packages/lhc/src/shared/context.ts:40-48); enqueue unconditionally registers ctx.onCommit(() => fireSchedulerPoke(ctx.threadId)) (packages/lhc/src/tech-utils/work-queue/index.ts:136); the background scheduler responds to the poke by draining (packages/lhc/src/scheduler.ts:315-319). Result: after `createSdk({mode:"background"})` then `createSdk({mode:"manual"})`, work queued via the manual SDK runs without any drain call, through the stale scheduler's provider and config — violating AC-1.7 ('queued work accumulates durably and does not run until the drain operation is invoked'). Reviewer-2 reproduced it end-to-end: w-m1-prompt_smoothing-v1 queued via the manual SDK drained with no manual drain invocation. Retained blocking per the conservative rule: the code confirms rather than disproves the blocker; assumption A3 narrows real-world exposure but the design itself contemplates multiple SDK constructions per process.

blockingFindings.title: Deleted tool results still determine tool-call outcomes through the unfiltered pairing read and an uncascaded counterpart summary
blockingFindings.evidence: Confirmed in code at every step of reviewer-2's claimed path. (1) findPairedBlock joins message with no deleted_at IS NULL (packages/lhc/src/domains/messages/internal/forms.ts:163-178) — an unsanctioned exception to tech design Part 3b's deleted-read filter rule, which names exactly two exceptions (event read-back, mutation validation's filtered existence check), not the pairing read. (2) toolCallSummaryHandler stamps the summary's outcome from that read (packages/lhc/src/domains/messages/internal/handlers.ts:98-105), so an explicit requeue of tool_call_summary after the paired tool_result is deleted rebuilds outcome 'succeeded' from a record no longer in the readable record — against AC-2.4's mechanical rule (no paired result → unknown) read with AC-6.1 (a deleted message no longer appears in reads). (3) cascadeMessageDelete drops the deleted message's own forms and clears only upward (turn, chunk) — the paired call's summary on a different message is never cleared (packages/lhc/src/domains/messages/internal/cascade.ts:209-215). (4) Composition prefers the ready summary's stale metadata over its own record-derived outcome fallback (packages/lhc/src/domains/turns/internal/compose.ts:150-153), so the delete cascade's own turn-rendering rebuild republishes the stale 'succeeded' while the rendering's membership correctly excludes the deleted result. The read-filter half is an unambiguous defect; the cascade half sits on a spec conflict between AC-6.2's 'nothing else changes' and AC-2.8's pair-as-source rule, carried as an unresolved item for a ruling.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Mutation and requeue operations bypass the SDK-injected clock
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: Confirmed: five sites call runInTransaction(db, () => new Date(), threadId, ...) — messages/index.ts:331, 421, 503 and turns/index.ts:356, 433 — so deleted_at stamps and requeued items' queuedAt use wall time regardless of SdkConfig.clock, which governs only drain/scheduler paths. Deterministic time injection does not extend to the mutation surfaces.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Deterministic provider is the only registered production provider
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: Confirmed: src/providers/registry.ts registers exactly one name ('deterministic'). Real adapters are explicitly out of epic scope and DD-11 sanctions the double's registry placement with no default, so this is by design — but until a real adapter lands, lhc work drain in production can only produce marked deterministic artifacts, selected by explicit operator opt-in.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Thrown handler errors are converted to retryable attempts
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: Confirmed at scheduler.ts:139-145: drainOpenDb catches a throwing handler and routes it through failAttempt as { retryable: true }, consuming retry budget before landing failed. The error contract says bugs throw and are not contract outcomes; this deliberately softens that to protect the queue from wedging (documented in place). Reasonable trade-off, but a deterministic handler bug is retried twice before surfacing.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Inconsistent attempts accounting between terminal paths
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: Confirmed: the unknown-kind terminal path stamps attempts: item.attempts (scheduler.ts:119-125) while the blocked-source terminal path stamps attempts: item.attempts + 1 (scheduler.ts:159-165). Cosmetic — the value only feeds the drain report and the form's failure metadata, and unknown-kind items never ran a handler — but the asymmetry is undocumented.

unresolvedItems: Cascade contract ruling needed for paired tool-call/tool-result dependencies: AC-6.2's exhaustive cascade scope ('nothing else changes') conflicts with AC-2.8's pair-as-source model. Decide whether deleting (or editing) one half of a call/result pair must clear and requeue the counterpart's summary, and update the epic's cascade-scope table either way. The findPairedBlock deleted-read filter fix is unambiguous and should not wait on this ruling.

Design ruling needed on the mode-isolation fix shape for EPIC-02-BLOCK-001: clear the process-global seams on manual-mode construction, scope the poke/touch seams per SDK instance, or refuse multi-SDK construction per process — all small, but the choice affects the documented multi-SDK semantics in sdk.ts.

crossStoryFindings: The story chain composes into one coherent mechanism with no reimplementation across stories: enqueue (Story 0) is the single creation point for derived_form rows, completion is UPDATE-only and source-version-checked in the queue util (Story 1), handlers return form writes as data (Stories 2-3), report/requeue join the same live work_item rows (Story 4), and mutations reuse the identical enqueue/supersede/version machinery (Stories 5-6).

DD-8's one-cascade rule held across stories: messages/internal/cascade.ts serves edit, message delete, and turn delete; turns.deleteTurn reaches it only through the messages domain's public surface (applyTurnDeleteCascade), and the boundary script confirms no cross-domain internal imports anywhere.

The deleted-read filter rule is applied consistently at every read site introduced across Stories 3-6: readMessages, readMutableMessage, readMemberMessages, readMemberProjections, readChunkRows, readTurns (both membership and turn rows), and readMutableTurn all append deleted_at IS NULL; the two sanctioned exceptions (event read-back and the handlers' readMessageSource) are deliberate and documented in place.

Drain report dispositions match DD-1's five-disposition contract exactly across the scheduler, queue util, and mutation results: done/stale_discarded/failed_terminal appear only in drain reports, superseded appears only on MutationResult, and terminal rows are deleted in the same transaction that records their outcome.

Work-item identity (w-<sourceId>-<kind>-v<sourceVersion>) is honored consistently by intake queueing, the AC-2.8 late-result requeue, both owners' repair requeues, and the mutation cascade's replacement enqueues, so the DD-3 stale-discard truth table holds at every write path I traced.

All implementation-time deviations are recorded and ruled in the team impl log (5 in Story 0, 7 in Story 1, 5 in Story 2, 3 in Story 3, the rejected-then-fixed AC-4.7 set in Story 4, 4 in Story 5, 2 in Story 6); I found no unrecorded drift between the code and the rulings.
architectureFindings: Module placement matches the tech design with two approved, recorded renames: turn handlers live in turns/internal/derive.ts rather than handlers.ts (Story 3 ruling), and the scheduler poke/touch seams live in shared/context.ts rather than the scheduler module to avoid an import cycle (Story 0 ruling, DD-5 semantics preserved).

Migration v5 implements the tech-design schema faithfully, including the F-02 backfill of pending form rows for pre-v5 queued items, plus the approved deviation that idx_work_item_queue omits rowid (SQLite forbids rowid in index definitions; claimNext's ORDER BY rowid preserves head-first semantics).

claimNext is the single atomic UPDATE under BEGIN IMMEDIATE specified in Part 3b, with the head re-read classifying empty/in_flight/waiting and the reclaim CASE incrementing attempts; the never-skip-ahead rule is structural, not procedural.

Provider calls never run inside a transaction: handlers receive openDb() for short reads, return form writes as data, and the queue util owns the completion transaction; the onApplied hook makes chunk placement and summary enqueues ride the same completion commit, so a crash leaves either a placed turn with queued summaries or nothing.

The chunk close policy implements DD-9's accumulation rule (close at accumulated + incoming >= target with the incoming turn starting the next chunk, single turn >= max closes its own chunk, empty chunks always accept) over stored projected-token values only, which is what makes TC-3.9 replay determinism hold.

The tech design said the boundary script would gain a scheduler allowed-import line; none was added because none is needed — scheduler.ts imports only domain public indexes, which the existing rules permit. The protection the design wanted exists; the specific mechanism was moot.

Minor drift: createSdk's injected clock governs drain and scheduler timestamps, but the mutation and requeue operations construct their own wall clock (runInTransaction(db, () => new Date(), ...)) for deleted_at and queuedAt stamps, so deterministic time injection does not extend to the mutation surfaces (see non-blocking finding E02-NB-001).
epicCoverageAssessment: Epic gate pnpm run verify-all passed from packages/lhc with exit 0: 29 test files, 231 tests, including the LHC_PROCESS_SUITE=1 spawned-process suite covering the architecture-risk fixtures (TC-1.3 SIGKILL restart survival, TC-1.4 cross-process claim exclusion).

All 46 TC ids from the epic appear verbatim in test titles across the suites (TC-1.1 through TC-6.8, plus Epic 01's TC-2.9 kind-gate amendment), matching the test plan's file mapping; the suite grew from Epic 01's 118 tests to 231, exceeding the plan's 60-70 estimate.

All 47 ACs trace to implemented behavior I read directly: queue execution and both host modes (scheduler.ts, work-queue), message derivation with mechanically stamped outcomes (handlers.ts, outcome.ts), turn composition with gap recording and deterministic chunking (derive.ts, compose.ts, chunks.ts), report/repair with blocked refusal and requeue idempotency (both owners' index.ts and forms.ts), and the three mutations with one-transaction cascade, supersede, and stale-write fencing (cascade.ts, store.ts).
The four architecture-risk tests named by the test plan (TC-1.3, TC-1.4, TC-5.4, TC-3.9) are all present and green in the gate run.

CLI parity is real: every SDK surface (drain, report, requeue, edit, delete message, delete turn) has a CLI command that calls the same domain operation with the same validation and result JSON, and the CLI drain assembles a manual-mode SDK through createSdk rather than an in-process shortcut.
productionPathFindings: No fake adapters, stubs, placeholders, or TODO/FIXME markers exist anywhere in src/; every handler, mutation, and read path is real execution against real SQLite state.

The deterministic provider ships in production source (src/providers/deterministic.ts) and is registered in the production named-provider registry. This is explicitly sanctioned by DD-11 and an approved Story 1 ruling: it is selectable only by explicit name (--provider deterministic / LHC_PROVIDER=deterministic), is never a default, and exists so spawned-CLI tests exercise the production resolution seam. A drain without a resolvable provider fails with provider_not_configured naming the flag and env var — fail-closed, never a silent no-op.

The deterministic provider is currently the ONLY registered named provider, so a production CLI drain can only produce marked deterministic artifacts today. This is consistent with the epic's explicit scope exclusion (real provider adapters are out of scope; this epic ships the seam and the double), but operators should understand real inference requires a future adapter registration.

Test seams compiled into production modules: setIntakeWalkHook and setIntakeClock in intake-stream/internal/pipeline.ts (Epic 01 carryover, set only through test fixtures, explicit-argument-wins), and Scheduler.testPassCount plus the passes counter in scheduler.ts (documented test-only observability, not API). All are inert in production assembly and documented in place; none fakes an execution path.

Background-mode scheduling is gated fail-closed on hasAnyHandler so an empty handler map can never turn queued rows into failed_terminal; in the shipped assembly both domains register real handlers, so the gate is always open in production.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Mutation and requeue operations bypass the SDK-injected clock
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: messages.edit, messages.deleteMessage, messages.requeue, turns.requeue, and turns.deleteTurn all call runInTransaction(db, () => new Date(), threadId, ...) — deleted_at stamps and requeued items' queuedAt use wall time regardless of SdkConfig.clock, which governs only drain/scheduler paths (and intake has its own setIntakeClock seam). Deterministic time injection therefore does not extend to the mutation surfaces.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Process-global scheduler seams not cleared by a later manual-mode SDK
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: createSdk installs setSchedulerPoke/setThreadTouch only in background mode and a later background SDK supersedes an earlier one (documented), but a manual-mode SDK constructed after a background one leaves the previous background scheduler installed — enqueues through the manual SDK would still poke the stale scheduler and drain with the old provider/config. Low real-world impact under assumption A3 (one host per process), but the background-then-manual sequence is unhandled.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Deterministic provider is the only registered production provider
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: src/providers/registry.ts registers exactly one name ('deterministic'). Real adapters are explicitly out of epic scope and DD-11 sanctions the double's registry placement with no default, so this is by design — but until a real adapter lands, lhc work drain in production can only produce marked deterministic artifacts, selected by explicit operator opt-in.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Thrown handler errors are converted to retryable attempts
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: drainOpenDb catches a throwing handler and routes it through failAttempt as { retryable: true }, consuming retry budget before landing failed. The error contract says bugs throw and are not contract outcomes; this deliberately softens that to protect the queue from wedging (documented in scheduler.ts). The trade-off is reasonable but means a deterministic handler bug is retried twice before surfacing.

nonBlockingFindings.title: Inconsistent attempts accounting between terminal paths
nonBlockingFindings.evidence: The blocked-source terminal path stamps attempts: item.attempts + 1 while the unknown-kind terminal path stamps attempts: item.attempts (scheduler.ts lines 119-125 vs 158-165). Cosmetic: the value only feeds the drain report and the form's failure metadata, and unknown-kind items never ran a handler, but the asymmetry is undocumented.

crossStoryFindings: Manual/background mode isolation is not preserved across SDK instances: a background SDK installs process-wide scheduler hooks and a later manual SDK does not clear them, so manual intake can drain automatically without an explicit drain call.

Deletion flow does not fully compose with paired tool-call/tool-result derivation: deleted tool results are excluded from turn membership but can still be read by the pairing query, and stale tool-call summary metadata can survive into rebuilt turn renderings.
architectureFindings: SDK mode selection drifts from the architecture contract because scheduler execution is controlled through process-global mutable hooks instead of being isolated to the SDK instance that chose background mode.

The deleted-read filter discipline misses the tool pairing read path, and the mutation cascade does not repair paired counterpart summaries even though Flow 2 makes the paired message a source dependency.
epicCoverageAssessment: Both required gates pass, and the implemented stories have broad test coverage, but the coverage misses cross-SDK mode isolation and delete/edit cases where a tool-call summary depends on a paired tool result.
productionPathFindings: No silent fake provider default was found: CLI drain requires --provider or LHC_PROVIDER, and the deterministic provider is explicit-only.
Material production-path issue found: manual mode can execute through a background scheduler left by a prior SDK in the same process.
Material production-path issue found: tool pairing can read deleted messages and produce real ready forms with outcomes derived from deleted records.

blockingFindings.title: Manual SDK mode can auto-drain after background SDK construction
blockingFindings.evidence: Verified by constructing a background SDK, then a manual SDK in the same process, ingesting one prompt through the manual SDK, and observing the queued work disappear without calling manual drain: queuedImmediately contained w-m1-prompt_smoothing-v1, then queuedAfterWait was empty and a ready smoothed_prompt form existed. Code path: src/sdk.ts installs setSchedulerPoke and setThreadTouch for background mode but manual mode does not clear them; src/tech-utils/work-queue/index.ts fires the global scheduler poke on enqueue; src/domains/threads/internal/create.ts fires the global thread touch; src/scheduler.ts responds by draining.

blockingFindings.title: Deleted tool results can still determine tool-call outcomes
blockingFindings.evidence: Verified by creating a turn with a tool_call and paired tool_result, draining, deleting the tool_result, draining again, and observing rebuilt turn rendering metadata still report the tool_call outcome as succeeded even though the live membership no longer includes the result. Requeuing the tool_call_summary after deletion still rebuilt outcome succeeded. Code path: src/domains/messages/internal/forms.ts findPairedBlock joins message without m.deleted_at IS NULL; src/domains/messages/internal/handlers.ts stamps tool_call_summary outcome from that pair; src/domains/turns/internal/compose.ts trusts ready summary metadata; src/domains/messages/internal/cascade.ts clears the deleted message and upward turn forms but does not clear the paired counterpart summary.

unresolvedItems: The cascade contract needs a ruling or update for paired tool-call/tool-result dependencies: the current delete cascade description focuses on the deleted message's upward chain, while the derivation architecture makes the paired counterpart a real source dependency.
